project.title: Continuous RC with live input changes
project.question: Does a capacitor keep its charge while the simulation pauses?
project.notes:
Expected: Set V1 to 5 V in Live inputs: the capacitor charges from its current voltage. Pause freezes time and state; resume continues the same exponential trajectory.
Try: Pause after charging, change V1 to 0 V, then Step or Resume. The capacitor discharges from its retained voltage rather than restarting at zero.
assumptions: Coordinated transient uses backward Euler for R/C/L and independent sources. Reduce maximum step to check numerical convergence.
Digital events, converter sampling and analog state share one causal time axis; no physical metastability, noise, power supply or device loading model is implied.

engine.name: CircuitBench coordinated transient
engine.package: CircuitBench stateful MNA and event kernel
engine.execution: Stateful modified nodal analysis and incremental digital events in an isolated worker
engine.coupling: Causal shared timeline; analog trial-step threshold localization; digital events and converter samples create analog breakpoints
engine.limitations: R/C/L and independent V/I sources only in the analog partition. Fixed maximum step with backward-Euler numerical damping; no transistor, diode, opamp, switch, noise or thermal model.

sampling.description: Stateful coordinated transient. Absolute simulation times; only the bounded recent window is retained. Its first digital value is a boundary state, not a new transition. Capacitor, inductor, clock and digital state continue across chunks and pauses.

bridgeAssumptions: The coordinated analog subset is R/C/L and independent V/I sources; backward Euler introduces step-dependent numerical damping.
